title: Set Resource Limits and Observe QoS
description: Deploy Pods with different resource settings and check their QoS classes.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Understand the three QoS classes by creating Pods with different resource configurations.

### Steps
1. Create a Pod YAML `guaranteed-pod.yaml` with one container that has equal requests and limits for CPU and memory (e.g., `cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi` both in requests and limits).
2. Create a Pod YAML `burstable-pod.yaml` with requests lower than limits, e.g., `requests: cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi`, `limits: cpu: 200m, memory: 256Mi`.
3. Create a Pod YAML `besteffort-pod.yaml` with no resources specified at all.
4. Apply all three Pods.
5. For each, run `kubectl describe pod <name> | grep QoS` and note the class (Guaranteed, Burstable, BestEffort).
6. Clean up by deleting all three Pods.
hints: Guaranteed requires every container to have both CPU and memory requests and limits, and they must be equal.
Burstable: at least one container has a request or limit, but not all are equal.
BestEffort: no resources section at all.
expectedOutput: Each Pod shows its respective QoS Class in the describe output.
solutionCode:
# guaranteed-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: guaranteed-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: "128Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: "128Mi"
---
# burstable-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: burstable-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "100m"
        memory: "128Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "200m"
        memory: "256Mi"
---
# besteffort-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: besteffort-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
